newsitem.title: USA: NY Gov sees "excellent chance" for bills' approval.
newsitem.headline: NY Gov sees "excellent chance" for bills' approval.

text.p: New York State Gov George Pataki on Tuesday said there was an "excellent chance" two major bills for New York City, one to extend a tax levy and one to set up a new borrowing authority, would be approved.

"I think there's an excellent chance now of passing both the safe cities extender (the tax bill) and the infrastructure financing authority bill," Pataki told reporters after meeting with top New York State legislators, whom he recalled for a special session that started Tuesday.

Pataki, a Republican, qualified his optimism, saying minor differences remained. Talks broke down late Monday when New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani sought more flexibility in spending the tax revenues than the Assembly Speaker, who wanted the city to hire about 750 recruits for a total of around 38,300, a level that now has been agreed.
Giuliani told reporters at City Hall that, while he was not sure the 12.5 percent personal income tax extender would be approved Tuesday, he could accept a plan being discussed.
"There's a proposal on the table now that could work," he said.

Assembly Speaker Sheldon Silver (D-Manhattan) who had wanted to only extend the tax levy for one year after it ends on December 31, said the sides agreed to keep it in place for two years. Pataki, Giuliani and the Republican-led Senate all had wanted to extend the tax for four years.

The Republican mayor agreed to go ahead with a plan to spend $550 million of the tax revenues over two years for school construction, Pataki said. The New York City personal income tax surcharge is expected to raise $455 million in the 1997 fiscal year and $473 million in the following year.
